claims.statement: The 2024 Construction Products Regulation applies to used products within scope and explicitly discusses increased reuse and future harmonised specifications.
The Regulation distinguishes products directly reused in a construction work from products placed on the market again, making legal classification central to the model.

contrary_evidence: The official text notes that the second-hand construction-products market is not well developed and requirements have varied.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: exclusive salvage clauses with demolition contractors and property managers; buyer demand through remanufacturers and construction distributors.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: clear 30 lots in year 1, reach 3 million PLN annual gross merchandise margin by year 4, build 3 million PLN owner equity and cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-11.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-3 hours per day after local inspection and logistics are delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 25%-50% gross margin after inspection, storage, handling, breakage and transport.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 12-24 months if inventory is pre-sold and storage days stay low.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 12%-25% transaction take rate or 20%-40% resale spread on pre-sold lots.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat across contractor project pipelines; usable yield and buyer recurrence are unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Condition, removal cost and resale outcomes improve lot selection and build buyer trust
fingerprint.customer: Deconstruction contractors disposing of recoverable components and professional buyers seeking verified used supply
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Supply is embedded in demolition contracts; demand is syndicated to repeat professional buyers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Rights-secured, inspected and pre-sold component lots with managed removal and logistics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A buyer pays at lot transfer; the exchange retains a fee or spread
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A renovation or demolition schedule makes reusable components available before mixed-waste removal

founder_fit: Analytical selection can limit physical inventory.
A regional pilot can use contractor relationships.
Marketplace operations can be systematised and delegated.
risks: Unsafe or misclassified products create liability.
Removal and logistics erase resale value.
First-refusal contracts may yield little usable material.

structure.control_point: Project-level first-refusal or consignment rights over named reusable components and a condition-to-resale dataset
structure.critical_dependency: Correct waste/product classification, buyer-accepted testing, safe removal and economical logistics

thesis: Win first-refusal or consignment rights from deconstruction contractors before reusable components become mixed waste, digitally inspect them, and pre-sell verified lots to contractors and remanufacturers. Contracted salvage supply, condition records and realised reuse outcomes are the control point.
title: Deconstruction First-Refusal Materials Exchange
uncertainties: Testing accepted by Polish buyers and insurers
